scenes.visual: Title card 'Survive, Then Give Birth' fades in over a row of small TEAL dots. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: TEAL dot = a living female, TEAL bar = l_x (fraction alive); GOLD dot = a daughter, GOLD number = m_x; GREY fading dot = a death; a DASHED horizontal line labelled '1 = replacement'. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Dots are simple cartoons; bars are computed from the lesson's table (n_x = 100, 80, 40, 10, 0; m_x = 0, 1, 2, 1).

scenes.tts: Here are a hundred newborn females, all born in the same season. Only ten of them will live to age three. Can this group still more than replace itself?
scenes.visual: A block of 100 TEAL dots (10 by 10) appears in a column labelled 'age 0'. On-screen text '100 newborn females'. To the right, empty columns labelled 'age 1', 'age 2', 'age 3'. A ghosted '10 reach age 3' tag flashes over the age-3 column, then a large question mark: 'More than replaces itself?'
scenes.narration: Here are a hundred newborn females, all born in the same season. Only ten of them will live to age three. Can this group still more than replace itself?

scenes.tts: A group born together is called a cohort. Follow it year by year, and at each age count how many are still alive. Those that die fade to grey.
scenes.visual: The block of dots steps right, column by column. At each step some dots turn GREY and fade out. Counts appear above each column as the dots arrive: '100', '80', '40', '10'. A label 'cohort' brackets the moving group.
scenes.narration: A group born together is called a cohort. Follow it year by year, and at each age count how many are still alive. Those that die fade to grey.

scenes.tts: Divide each count by the starting hundred. That fraction is ell sub x, the share of the cohort still alive at age x. Here it falls from one to a tenth.
scenes.caption: Divide each count by the starting hundred. That fraction is l_x, the share of the cohort still alive at age x. Here it falls from 1 to 0.1.
scenes.visual: Under each column a TEAL bar grows to its height: 1.0, 0.8, 0.4, 0.1 (computed, labelled 'l_x'). The division 'n_x / 100' sits briefly beside the first bar, then fades. The heading 'l_x = fraction alive at age x' stays at the left.
scenes.narration: Divide each count by the starting hundred. That fraction is l_x, the share of the cohort still alive at age x. Here it falls from 1 to 0.1.

scenes.tts: Survivors also give birth. Life tables like this usually count females only, so the births we count are daughters.
scenes.visual: Above the age-1 column, a few TEAL dots gain a small GOLD dot beside them. A banner reads 'births counted = daughters'.
scenes.narration: Survivors also give birth. Life tables like this usually count females only, so the births we count are daughters.

scenes.tts: At each age, m sub x is the average number of daughters born per living female. Here the averages are zero in the first year, then one, two, and one.
scenes.caption: At each age, m_x is the average number of daughters born per living female. Here the averages are 0 in the first year, then 1, 2, and 1.
scenes.visual: Under each column a GOLD number appears beside the TEAL bar: 'm_x = 0', '1', '2', '1', with a small tag 'average per female'. In the age-2 column every surviving TEAL dot sprouts two GOLD dots; in ages 1 and 3, one GOLD dot each.
scenes.narration: At each age, m_x is the average number of daughters born per living female. Here the averages are 0 in the first year, then 1, 2, and 1.

scenes.tts: Now the key step. A newborn female may not live to a given age. So her daughters there count only as far as survival allows. Multiply the share still alive by the daughters each one has. That is what an average newborn female can expect at that age.
scenes.visual: In each column the TEAL bar and the GOLD number slide together and merge into a small TEAL-and-GOLD tile labelled 'l_x x m_x'. The tiles read '0', '0.8', '0.8', '0.1' on screen.
scenes.narration: Now the key step. A newborn female may not live to a given age. So her daughters there count only as far as survival allows. Multiply the share still alive by the daughters each one has. That is what an average newborn female can expect at that age.

scenes.tts: Add those pieces across her whole life. The total is R zero, the daughters left by an average newborn female. Here it comes to one point seven.
scenes.caption: Add those pieces across her whole life. The total is R0, the daughters left by an average newborn female. Here it comes to 1.7.
scenes.visual: The four tiles lift and stack into one vertical bar at the right labelled 'R0'. A DASHED line at height 1 runs behind it. The bar tops out at 1.7; on-screen text 'R0 = 0 + 0.8 + 0.8 + 0.1 = 1.7'. A small counted check fades in below: '80 + 80 + 10 = 170 daughters from 100 founders'.
scenes.narration: Add those pieces across her whole life. The total is R0, the daughters left by an average newborn female. Here it comes to 1.7.

scenes.tts: The dashed line marks one. At one, each female just replaces herself. Above it, each generation is larger than the last. Below it, each is smaller. So yes, this cohort more than replaces itself.
scenes.visual: The DASHED line brightens with labels: above it 'growth', on it 'replacement', below it 'decline'. The R0 bar at 1.7 glows above the line; a check mark answers the opening question mark.
scenes.narration: The dashed line marks one. At one, each female just replaces herself. Above it, each generation is larger than the last. Below it, each is smaller. So yes, this cohort more than replaces itself.

scenes.tts: Now give the cohort a hard first winter. Only half as many females reach age one. What happens to R zero?
scenes.caption: Now give the cohort a hard first winter. Only half as many females reach age one. What happens to R0?
scenes.visual: Snowflakes drift over the gap between the age-0 and age-1 columns. The age-1 column visibly loses half its TEAL dots (80 to 40 on screen). The R0 bar shows a question mark at its top.
scenes.narration: Now give the cohort a hard first winter. Only half as many females reach age one. What happens to R0?

scenes.visual: Hold on the question mark over the R0 bar and the dashed line. Small on-screen text 'Predict: what happens to R0?'

scenes.tts: Keep every later survival chance and birth rate the same. Every female alive at two or three first had to survive that winter. So the share alive halves at every later age, not just at age one.
scenes.visual: A small tag 'later rates unchanged' clips onto the columns for ages 1 to 3. Then the TEAL bars at ages 1, 2 and 3 each shrink to half, one after another: 0.8 to 0.4, 0.4 to 0.2, 0.1 to 0.05 (computed). A thin arrow runs from the winter snowflakes through all three columns.
scenes.narration: Keep every later survival chance and birth rate the same. Every female alive at two or three first had to survive that winter. So the share alive halves at every later age, not just at age one.

scenes.tts: Every piece of R zero halves, so R zero halves too, to below the line. Survival to any age is the product of every year before it. So a loss early in life cuts every later birth.
scenes.caption: Every piece of R0 halves, so R0 halves too, to below the line. Survival to any age is the product of every year before it. So a loss early in life cuts every later birth.
scenes.visual: The tiles shrink to '0', '0.4', '0.4', '0.05' and restack; the R0 bar drops from 1.7 to 0.85, now below the DASHED line, and turns from glowing to dim. On-screen text 'l_3 = p_0 x p_1 x p_2' appears briefly beside the bars.
scenes.narration: Every piece of R0 halves, so R0 halves too, to below the line. Survival to any age is the product of every year before it. So a loss early in life cuts every later birth.

scenes.tts: Two cautions. R zero is counted per generation, not per year. A yearly rate also needs the length of a generation. And R zero predicts long-run growth only if the rates stay fixed, and nobody arrives or leaves.
scenes.caption: Two cautions. R0 is counted per generation, not per year. A yearly rate also needs the length of a generation. And R0 predicts long-run growth only if the rates stay fixed, and nobody arrives or leaves.
scenes.visual: Two cards slide in beside the bars: 'per generation, not per year' (a clock icon struck through) and 'fixed rates, no migration' (a fence drawn around the cohort, arrows in and out crossed out).
scenes.narration: Two cautions. R0 is counted per generation, not per year. A yearly rate also needs the length of a generation. And R0 predicts long-run growth only if the rates stay fixed, and nobody arrives or leaves.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot holding a stacked TEAL-and-GOLD bar beside the DASHED line. Line: 'Survival times births, summed over a life: above one means growth.'
